purpose: personal account of renaming and restructuring Alexey's AI agents course into AI Engineering Buildcamp

required_facts.fact: The course was renamed, significantly restructured, and given expanded optional framework coverage after first-cohort feedback.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 3-9: the three changes and their reason are stated.

required_facts.fact: Around 90 percent of the material was being re-recorded for the second cohort, starting in two days.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 11: re-recording scope and timing are given.

required_facts.fact: The new name was AI Engineering Buildcamp because it better represented hands-on AI systems built with an engineering mindset.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 15-17: the new name and rationale are described.

required_facts.fact: Participants were expected to build real systems, practice trade-offs, reliability, and maintainability, and finish with reusable results.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 19-24: participant outcomes are listed.

required_facts.fact: Participants began a Capstone in Week 1, refined it conceptually and through implementation, and spent the final two weeks building and polishing it.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 29: Capstone timing and progression are stated.

required_facts.fact: Homework included more than six guided mini-projects such as FAQ assistants, YouTube Q&A, documentation, coding, and deep research agents.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 31: mini-project count and examples are listed.

required_facts.fact: First-cohort feedback said the content was dense and valuable but the pace too fast.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 35-37: participant feedback is quoted.

required_facts.fact: The redesigned course was longer and less dense, with a main path around one framework and optional bonus material.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 39-46: the new structure and core/optional split are described.

required_facts.fact: The agents section began without a framework, implementing tool calling and control loops manually before introducing PydanticAI as the main framework.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 55-66: framework sequence and rationale are specified.

required_facts.fact: Optional material covered LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google Agent Development Kit, CrewAI, and alternative model providers.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 68-75: optional frameworks and providers are listed.

author_attribution: Attribute course decisions and participant feedback to Alexey and the first cohort as documented; preserve the stated focus on hands-on engineering.
